newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka forex market stagnates on dlr weakness.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka forex market stagnates on dlr weakness.

text.p: The Sri Lankan rupee remained untraded against the dollar on Monday morning due to the weakness of the greenback overseas and a lack of imports, dealers said.
At 0430 GMT the rupee stood at its opening level of 58.50 to the dollar.
"There is no speculative demand for dollars," a Deutsche Bank dealer said. "The lack of imports means there is no commercial demand (for the dollar)."
The Central Bank pushed down the dollar-rupee exchange rate by half a local cent in line with the U.S. unit's overseas weakness, fixing buying and selling rates at 58.2095 and 59.3855.
"Even if there is import covering later in the day, the dollar should not rise beyond about 58.60 because there are plenty of sellers," said the Deutsche Bank delaer.
The dollar's upside was seen limited as call money rates continued to be tight, dealers said.
Overnight call money was at 16 percent after opening at 15 percent, they said.
